headline: Review Box Cañon Falls and Hot Springs Access Rules
reservation: Access to Box Cañon Falls and the Ouray Hot Springs Pool requires daily admission or specific passes; verify current seasonal hours on official city pages. While town access is open, high-country Jeep roads and hiking trails toward Yankee Boy Basin are seasonal and managed by the US Forest Service. Guided tour and accommodation reservations should be secured months in advance for summer and fall peaks, as systems for backcountry use are subject to change.

days.title: Waterfalls and Valley Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Ouray Main Street

stops.name: Box Cañon Falls Park
stops.detail: Walk the suspended catwalks into a narrow quartzite canyon to view the dramatic 285-foot waterfall.

stops.name: Cascade Falls Park
stops.detail: Visit the lowest of a series of seven waterfalls, accessible via a short but steep walk from the eastern end of 8th Avenue.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; primarily walking within town limits
days.note: Stay on established trails as valley walls are exceptionally steep and prone to loose rock.

days.title: High Alpine Basins and Backroads
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from a local outfitter office

stops.name: Yankee Boy Basin
stops.detail: Explore a high-altitude glacial cirque known for summer wildflowers and views of Mount Sneffels.

stops.name: Ouray Perimeter Trail
stops.detail: Hike sections of this 6-mile loop that encircles the town, offering elevated perspectives of the Uncompahgre Gorge.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours; high-clearance 4WD essential for basin roads
days.note: High-altitude weather changes rapidly; plan to be below the tree line before afternoon thunderstorms arrive.

days.title: The Million Dollar Highway Scenic Loop
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM heading south on US 550

stops.name: Red Mountain Pass
stops.detail: Navigate the summit of the Million Dollar Highway, observing the vibrant iron-oxide-stained peaks and historic mining remains.

stops.name: Ironton Park
stops.detail: Stop at this high-mountain meadow and ghost town site for a level walk through mining history.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; road is winding with significant drop-offs and no guardrails
days.note: Check Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT) for pass closures due to weather or maintenance.

intel.title: Town and Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Street parking in downtown Ouray is limited during the July Fourth holiday and autumn foliage peak. Popular trailheads like the Perimeter Trail access points lack large lots; consider walking from town lodging when possible.

intel.title: Canyon Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is generally reliable within the town of Ouray but drops immediately upon entering the Uncompahgre National Forest. Download offline maps for all 4WD routes toward Camp Bird or Silverton.

intel.title: Mountain Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel is available in Ouray, but prices may reflect the remote location. For longer mountain loops, top off in Montrose or Ridgway before heading into the high passes.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Openings
intel.text: High-altitude passes typically remain snowed-in until late June or early July. Autumn colors usually peak in late September, but wind events can shorten the season overnight.

intel.title: Box Cañon Restrictions
intel.text: The falls area may have restricted access during heavy spring runoff for safety. Check the official city visitor center for current daily trail conditions.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at Montrose Regional Airport (MTJ) and drive 40 miles south on US 550. Stop in Ridgway for regional groceries before the final climb into the Ouray valley.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for town and US 550; however, a high-clearance 4WD is mandatory for alpine basins. Check rental contracts for 'off-pavement' exclusions.
plan.goldenHour: Switzerland of America Lookout on US 550; sunset varies greatly by ridgeline height.
